scenes.headline: How an agent drives a parametric CAD kernel
scenes.sub: SolidCraft: one command registry, an exact kernel, names that survive edits
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Datum! Let's see how SolidCraft lets an agent build a part, change a number, and get the same part back.

scenes.text: Every tool, the desktop, the browser and the MCP server, runs the same commands on an exact kernel, and features remember edges by name.
scenes.say: The idea: every front end runs the same commands on an exact kernel, and features remember edges by name, not by position.

steps.say: The agent talks to an MCP server with twenty one tools. Most work goes through one of them, execute.
Execute runs any command in the registry, the same commands the toolbar and scripts run.
Commands edit a feature timeline. Sketch dimensions and extrude depths are expressions of named parameters.
Change a parameter and the timeline rebuilds through solidcore, a Rust port of NVIDIA's SMLib kernel. STEP keeps the exact shape.

scenes.title: How a fillet finds its edge

left.title: By index
left.say: Stored by index, a fillet breaks quietly. One upstream hole renumbered five of eighteen untouched edges.

right.title: By name
right.say: SolidCraft stores the faces an edge separates, named from the kernel's own history, and says so when one is lost.

scenes.label: worst relative volume error over 12 exact rebuilds in OpenCascade
scenes.note: a coarse STL of the same part: 3.3e-4
scenes.say: Rebuilt twelve ways in an independent kernel, the exact part never drifted past the last digit of a double. A coarse mesh of it was off by three parts in ten thousand.

scenes.text: Give an agent an exact kernel, rollback, and names instead of indices, then check its part before exporting a mesh.

recap: One command registry for every front end
Edges stored by name, not index
scenes.say: To recap: one command registry, exact rebuilds from parameters, and edges stored by name.
